# Add volume-based pricing tiers to usage dimensions

Usage dimensions need an optional `tiers` array so high-volume usage can be billed at different unit prices. Each tier uses string fields `tierPosition`, `upperBound`, optional `tierName`, and optional `unitPrice`; `upperBound` is a numeric string or `"inf"`. Bounds must increase without overlap, align to `usageIncrement`, and leave `"inf"` only at the end. Every tier after the first requires `unitPrice`; an omitted first-tier price represents a free tier.

Tiered dimensions are mutually exclusive with `usageEntitlement`, `consumptionPrice`, and `overageAllowed: true`. Creation, update, and read APIs must validate, persist, replace, clear with `tiers: null`, and return the same tier objects. Billing must sort by numeric `tierPosition`, allocate usage across the inclusive bounds, divide quantities by `usageIncrement`, preserve price precision and currency conversion, and produce a distinct line item per consumed tier. Append `tierName` to the normal line-item name when present. Existing non-tiered dimensions and invoice behavior must remain unchanged.

One legacy case is especially important: a dimension with no `tiers`, no `consumptionPrice`, and no `usageEntitlement` is valid and contributes no invoice line items. Do not make tier support turn that unpriced dimension into an error or a synthetic charge.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure.

Implemented volume-based pricing tiers for usage dimensions.

**New files**
- `src/dimensions/dto/usageTier.dto.ts` — `UsageTier` model (`tierPosition`, `upperBound`, optional `tierName`/`unitPrice`, all strings) with swagger/class-validator metadata.
- `src/dimensions/dto/tiersValidator.ts` — `findTiersValidationError` (single source of truth), the `@ValidateTiers` class-validator decorator, plus `isTieredDimension`, `getSortedTiers`, `tierUpperBoundToNumber`. Enforces: non-empty array, integer/unique `tierPosition`, numeric-or-`"inf"` `upperBound`, strictly increasing bounds, alignment to `usageIncrement`, `"inf"` only on the highest tier, `unitPrice` required after the first tier (omitted first price = free tier, max 8 decimals), and mutual exclusivity with `usageEntitlement`, `consumptionPrice`, `overageAllowed: true`.

**API / persistence**
- `create-dimension.dto.ts:337` adds the validated, documented `tiers` field; the entity→DTO constructor returns the stored tiers and no longer assumes a price segment exists.
- `entitlementValidator.ts` — `ShouldSetConsumptionPrice` now requires the price to be *absent* for tiered dimensions (non-tiered behavior unchanged).
- `dimensions.entity.ts` — `Numerical` carries `tiers`, serialized as a JSON tag and parsed back on read.
- `dimensions.service.ts` — `transformDtoToEntityInput` normalizes/validates tiers, and drops `consumptionPrice`/`usageEntitlement`/`overageAllowed` for tiered dimensions; `mergeTierPricingForUpdate` replaces tiers on update, clears them with `tiers: null`, rejects conflicting fields sent in the same payload, and lets a new pricing model replace the old one.

**Billing**
- `Billing.allocateUsageAcrossTiers` sorts by numeric `tierPosition` and allocates usage across inclusive upper bounds, returning only consumed tiers.
- `Offering.addTieredLineItemsForUsage` emits one line item per consumed tier, dividing quantity by `usageIncrement`, using `Offering.convertPriceToUnitCost` (shared with the legacy path) to preserve price precision and currency conversion, honoring `freeDimensionOnInvoice` for free tiers, and appending `tierName` to the normal line-item name (`InvoiceLineItem.prepareLineItem`).
- Legacy case preserved: a dimension with no tiers, no `consumptionPrice` and no `usageEntitlement` is skipped (no error, no synthetic/NaN charge) instead of producing an invalid line item.

**Tests** (40 new, in `src/dimensions/dto/dimensionTiers.dto.spec.ts`, `src/dimensions/dimensionTiers.service.spec.ts`, `src/offering/entities/tieredUsageLineItems.spec.ts`) cover validation rules, create/read/update/clear round-trips through a fake Influx point store, allocation math, ordering, increments, free tiers, EUR precision, and the unpriced legacy dimension.

`npm run build` succeeds and `npm run test:ci -- --runInBand` passes 260/260 tests (220 pre-existing + 40 new); `eslint --quiet` is clean.
